transcript:
Meeting header
Date/Time: 2026-08-03 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marco Gutierrez (Redwood SE), Sara Li (FinTrust Eng Mgr), Ravi Patel (Platform Eng), Emilie Chen (Security)

Summary: Quick sync on Dedicated sizing for POC, review of last week's performance numbers, plan for autoscaling policies and burst capacity test. Agreed next steps: run a 2-hour 100 RPS burst benchmark, Redwood to send pricing and SOC2 docs, customer to confirm SLOs and traffic profile.

Topics: sizing, autoscaling policy, KV cache behavior, latency SLOs, burst planning, compliance docs, next benchmark date

Action items (recap at end): see metadata list above

Transcript:
[00:00] Lena Park: hey everybody, thanks for hopping on. quick agenda - 1 sizing review, autoscale policy options, and then we want to schedule the burst test. how's that sound?
[00:08] Sara Li: sounds good, lena. we had a look at the spreadsheet you sent. a couple of questions on tail latency numbers.
[00:12] Marco G: cool. i'll pull up the dashboard in a sec. the numbers we reported last week were from the 50 RPS steady state run plus a short 5-minute spike.
[00:22] Ravi Patel: yeah, and in our env we saw a couple of 95th percentiles creep up to 420 ms. for the smaller payloads we expect around 200 ms, so want to understand why the tail was high.
[00:34] Marco G: right, so two things - 1 first the warmup on the KV cache, we saw the KV cache not fully primed during the short spike which bumped latency, second, some requests hit a cold quantized path which adds ~80-120 ms.
[00:47] Emilie Chen: when you say KV cache, do you mean prefix caching? how does that behave in dedicated vs hosted? we need determinism for audits.
[00:56] Marco G: good question. on Redwood Dedicated the prefix/KV cache is sticky to the GPU pool instance groups. so if autoscale spins up a new worker, the new worker's cache is cold until warmed. we can configure longer sticky sessions or pre-warm with traffic.
[01:12] Sara Li: ok, so if we have bursts, spin-up could cause tail spikes. what are our autoscale options?
[01:18] Marco G: three levers - 1 minimum pool size, scale-up policy (aggressive vs smoothing), and burst capacity (reserved warm instances). for your workload i'd recommend min 2 instances for baseline, scaling threshold at 70% GPU utilization with a 30s evaluation window, and keep a small burst reserve of 1-2 GPUs for immediate handling.
[01:36] Ravi Patel: can you quantify that in terms of RPS? like 100RPS would need how many GPUs for our model?
[01:42] Marco G: based on the POC model (7B quantized profile) and your observed token length, 1 A40-equivalent GPU does ~120 - 1150 concurrent token throughput for short requests. to target p95 < 300 ms under 100 RPS burst, i'd recommend 3 GPUs in the pool with burst reserve to handle spikes.
[01:58] Sara Li: 3 GPUs - 1 got it. cost-sensitive question: how does that compare to hosted per-token cost? we need to build an ops estimate.
[02:06] Lena Park: good call. i'll send a cost comparison sheet - 1 dedicated committed vs hosted burst. committed gives better unit cost but you pay reservation; burst reserve is cheaper than overprovisioning full pool.
[02:18] Emilie Chen: from a security/compliance angle, we need details on data retention between instances and audit logs for the autoscaler. also key management - 1 KMS or HSM?
[02:29] Marco G: Dedicated supports KMS integration and customer-managed keys; we log autoscale events to the control plane audit log and can stream to your SIEM. i will attach the deployment checklist and SOC2/ISO excerpts.
[02:39] Emilie Chen: perfect, that helps.
[02:42] Sara Li: back to burst testing - 1 what's the recommended test? we want a realistic pattern: baseline 20 RPS for 30 minutes, then ramp to 100 RPS for 2 hours with 10% random spikes, then cool down.
[02:54] Marco G: that pattern makes sense. we'll do a 2-hour sustained burst with 10% jitter; we'll run it from our benchmark infra so we can correlate infra metrics. we recommend running with min pool size set to 2 and burst reserve 1, then repeat with min pool 3 to compare.
[03:10] Ravi Patel: when can you run it? this week? friday?
[03:13] Marco G: we can run Friday morning PST - 1 i'll need a thumbs up on the exact time and you'll need to allow the external runner IPs in the firewall.
[03:21] Lena Park: i'll follow up with the IPs. also i'll include the exact command and load profile in the notes.
[03:27] Sara Li: ok. i also want to confirm model fallbacks - 1 if a GPU pool is constrained do we have automatic fallback to a cheaper model?
[03:34] Marco G: yes, you can define routing policies. for POC we can setup an automatic fallback to a smaller quantized variant or to a hosted route. note fallbacks change semantics so include in SLO docs.
[03:45] Emilie Chen: and auditing those fallbacks? need to see logs showing fallback events.
[03:49] Marco G: that's in the rollout/audit logs, we'll include examples in the docs.
[03:54] Sara Li: one more - 1 slow start vs aggressive scale-up tradeoff. we prefer avoiding overreaction but also need to keep p95 low. any recommended setting?
[04:01] Marco G: for your workload, smoothing with a two-step scale (fast initial scale over 30s to add 1 GPU, then gradual over 3-5 minutes) balances tail latency and cost. the burst reserve handles the immediate spike.
[04:14] Ravi Patel: are pre-warm scripts available? could we pre-warm KV cache during business hours to reduce cold starts?
[04:20] Marco G: yes, you can configure pre-warm hooks - 1 run a synthetic workload to prime caches. we can provide a script that replays common prefixes.
[04:27] Sara Li: great. i want to make sure the benchmark will capture KV hit rates, cold-start counts, and per-token cost.
[04:34] Marco G: we'll capture GPU util, KV hit/miss, latency distribution, and token counts. we'll produce a dashboard link after the run.
[04:41] Lena Park: action items - 1 marco to run the test and share results; me to send pricing + SOC2 docs; emilie to confirm doc list; sara to share traffic traces. anything else?
[04:50] Emilie Chen: can we get a short writeup for the audit team that explains autoscale determinism and what logs look like?
[04:56] Marco G: yes, we'll produce a 1-pager with sample logs and retention guarantees.
[05:01] Sara Li: timeline - 1 after benchmark run we want a 48-hour window to review before deciding on charter to commit.
[05:08] Lena Park: understood. we'll aim to have the benchmark Friday and results by Monday.
[05:12] Ravi Patel: small note - 1 we use a mixed cloud infra, some workloads go through our VPC peering. any network considerations?
[05:18] Marco G: ensure MTU and NAT timeouts are standard; long-lived connections for streaming should be ok but we recommend connection pooling. we'll include network checklist.
[05:27] Sara Li: ok thanks, team.
[05:29] Lena Park: thanks everyone. i'll recap in email with the timing and attached docs.
[05:33] Emilie Chen: bye all.

End of meeting.

References mentioned: pricing spreadsheet (link sent in chat), benchmark dashboard (post-run), SOC2 excerpt (to be shared), pre-warm script (to be attached).
